title: Interface text
headline: The words themselves are in good order: 2,003 storefront keys in four languages and 29,040 admin texts in two, none missing, and only 34 keys nothing reads (0.1%). The bloat is in how they are loaded. 802 of 830 server entries and the proxy evaluate all 134 admin catalogue files and all four storefront languages at each cold start (about 80 to 105 ms and 13 MB here, a tenth of the start); admin pages hand whole areas to the browser (the product editor hands 204 KB where its parts name at most 65 KB); and 97 of 111 visitor routes load about 25 KB of cookie purposes and admin words no shopper reads. The empty commerce.ui_translations table is what one expects before opening and is no finding; its loader is: it asks every minute per instance today, and as written every cold start will read each translated language whole, one after another (about 135 KB, 6 to 13 ms and 0.4 MB a language). Four fixes are small and safe now (TX-4, TX-5, TX-8, TX-11), and the two structural ones (TX-1, TX-2) are cheapest before opening and before a third admin language adds about 1.5 MB to every function.

clean: The languages are complete and held by the compiler. Re-checked here key by key: nb, sv and da each have all 2,003 storefront keys and all 316 email keys, none missing, none extra; the admin's Norwegian has every one of the 29,040 English keys.

A shopper's document carries only what it shows: 7 to 32 catalogue texts in one language on the 12 measured pages (verified report). Storefront client components are typed with small label groups of BrowserMessages, not with Messages (my rg of the 'use client' files under src/app/s and src/components).

Choosing a language does not make pages dynamic. The language is in the address (resolveShop, /home/user/kaizen-store/src/server/shop.ts:42-49). Only the front door is decided per visitor, by a 307 in the proxy with Vary and no-store (/home/user/kaizen-store/src/proxy.ts:110-116). The admin reads the account's choice.

The catalogues' typing is the cheap kind: plain object literals, one Widen<typeof en> per area, each Norwegian file annotated with it. Measured alone it is about 125 MB and under a second. Retyping the catalogues would not move the 5 GB heap, so no cheaper typing is proposed; a missing key stays a compile error as it is.
Dead text is about 0.1% of keys and no catalogue is an orphan: every one of the 67 areas is in the registry and has readers.
Repeated labels (Save, Name, Cancel) are 24% of the admin's keys but 7% of its characters, and they let one area be handed to a page alone. Leave them.

The admin's English fallback is fetched per area only when needed (D540, /home/user/kaizen-store/src/components/admin/admin-text-later.ts) and a signed-in test fails on any screen that needs it. Only common and sign-in English are compiled into the admin's first scripts.

The AI-translated interface (commerce.ui_translations, D111) costs no AI call at night for a language nobody asked for (/home/user/kaizen-store/src/server/ui-nightly.ts:53-63). Its table being empty is expected before opening and is no reason to change the feature. Nothing else in src reads the table on a request path (rg ui_translations: the loader, the platform admin's tools and the nightly job).
The glossary (/home/user/kaizen-store/src/lib/i18n-glossary.ts, 852 lines) is imported by tests only (rg: no non-test importer). It costs nothing at run time.

Kaizena Flow's own chrome words (messages/platform-en.ts and platform-nb.ts, 32 and 33 KB) reach no visitor client code: client parts take typed slices such as PlatformMessages["docs"]["guide"] as props (my client import graph).

The four small browser-text files loading together with a page's first scripts is a written, tested decision (D212, /home/user/kaizen-store/docs/performance.md:52-60: loading one language on its own once lost a press). It costs a shopper about 4.6 KB gzip. Leave it until a fifth hand-written language is added.

Norwegian-only files nav.nb.ts (42.8 KB) and pages.nb.ts (61.2 KB) are a second way of translating (by English sentence and by page id), held by admin-nav-words.test.ts. They are server-side cost only and are counted in TX-1; not worth a change of their own.

findings.title: Every server instance, and the proxy, evaluates all 134 admin catalogue files and all four storefront languages when it starts
findings.evidence: admin-text.ts imports all 134 area files statically into one table; adminText(lang, area) reads one entry. In the build, 802 of 830 route entries and the proxy load a chunk with 100 or more of the 134 area-languages, and a heap probe finds 132 of them evaluated in /api/visit and in the proxy (verified report). My own count: 35 files outside the admin import the registry by value (32 in src/server, src/lib/two-step.ts, src/lib/work-text.ts, src/app/api/platform/editor/route.ts). Between them they read 18 areas, each by a literal name; 12 of the 35 read only staffEmails. The proxy reaches the registry through holding.ts, auth.ts and two-step.ts, which needs the signIn area. The static closure of src/proxy.ts is 1,311 source modules and holds 135 of the 136 catalogue files. If the 35 files read their own areas, the closure holds 37 catalogue files, 33% of the catalogues' source bytes: 16 files are the areas those files name, the others come through 37 lib and server modules that import an English catalogue directly, 21 of the 68 such modules only for a default argument.
findings.cost: Per cold start of a server instance and of the proxy: about 2.9 MB of catalogue code read and about 80 to 105 ms and 13 MB of heap to evaluate it (this machine, not Vercel), for words a storefront, API or cron request never shows. That is about a tenth of the measured cold start. The build writes the set out 12 times (35.6 MB). Each further admin language adds about 1.5 MB to every function. It will be felt more after opening: more stores mean more instances and more cold starts in front of shoppers.
findings.who_pays: The server at every cold start and in every instance's memory; a shopper whose request starts a new proxy or page instance; the build.

findings.title: Admin pages hand whole areas of words to the browser in every document
findings.evidence: adminTexts(lang, areas) serialises each named area whole into the page. Measured documents (verified report): the product editor's holds 233 KB of whole areas in 416 KB (56%), the page builder's 304 KB in 572 KB (53%); of 195 hand-down sites with a literal list the median is 28.9 KB and 17 are over 100 KB. My own static count for three pages: the product editor hands product, products, fields, builder and website, 204,116 bytes of English JSON, and the client parts in its import graph name at most 65,307 of them. On the product, order and customer pages the only readers of the builder area are rich-text-editor.tsx and text-styles.tsx, which read its richText and textStyles groups: 2,847 of the 74,940 bytes handed. The product editor reads two groups of website (1,616 of 47,127 bytes). The order page hands 163,851 bytes and names at most 75,642. Every signed-in document carries common, setup and shell, and for an owner assistant: 34.0 KB raw / 11.7 KB gzip in English, 45.3 / 15.3 in Norwegian. No file in src calls useAdminText("setup"): its 6.9 KB is read by nothing in the browser. Across the admin, 33 files read the builder area 160 times; 115 reads name one group on the call.
findings.cost: Over half of the raw bytes of the product editor's and the page builder's documents and a third or more of several list pages'. A page's own areas are sent again on each navigation to it and each redraw after a save. The server serialises them on every request. Nothing measures a document's words today, so the amount grows with every text added to a large area.
findings.who_pays: An owner's browser on every admin page view; the server per request.

findings.title: Every server instance asks the table of AI translations every minute, whether or not it serves such a language
findings.evidence: The statement's caller is refresh() in ui-text.ts:57-62. instrumentation.ts awaits startUi() when an instance starts (Next: register must complete before requests are taken), and startUi() then runs refresh() every 60 s for the instance's life (lines 106-116). It is not cached because it is the cache check: each instance keeps the languages in its own memory so the synchronous t() never waits, and nothing tells an instance that a language changed. Production: 278,393 calls in 78 days, 2.5 a minute. The answer to the owner's question is yes: the table is empty because no store sells in an AI-translated language yet. The finding does not need it to be empty: the check runs per instance per minute whatever the instance serves.
findings.cost: About 3,570 small queries a day today and one round trip before the first request of each new instance. Each live instance adds 1,440 a day, so it grows with traffic, not with use of the feature. Once languages exist, each check also counts every row of the table (1,863 rows a language). The statement's time is not in the statistics; small.
findings.who_pays: The database and its connection pool; the server at every cold start.
fix_steps: 1. In src/server/ui-text.ts (or the reader file split out of it, see notes) add used: boolean to the state. uiTextsFor(lang) (line 127), which the storefront layout already calls for every market (layout.tsx:131), sets state().used = true when the language is not built in. It reads no clock and no database: Next guards Date.now() while a page is prerendered (08-caching.md:331), and the written rule forbids reading the texts while rendering.

2. Replace setInterval in startUi() (lines 109-114) with a setTimeout chain. Each tick: note and clear used, run refresh() unless one is in flight, then schedule the next tick after FRESH_MS (60 s) if the instance was asked for a translated language since the last tick, and after a new IDLE_MS (600,000) if not. Keep timer.unref().

3. Leave the read at start (line 108) and ensureUi() before emails (shopper-emails.ts:108, notifications.ts:367) as they are. Do not call ensureUi() from a page: it reads Date.now() (line 99) and may wait on the database.
4. Update the module comment (ui-text.ts:19-27) and docs/rules/storefront.md:69-71: an instance looks for changes each minute while it serves a translated language and every ten minutes otherwise.
tests_and_rules: New unit test with fake timers and a counting stub for readDb(): no call of uiTextsFor() for a translated language gives one refresh in ten minutes; a call gives one each minute until a minute passes without one.
src/server/languages.int.test.ts:123 uses reloadUi(), which is unchanged.
Rule kept: 'never read the texts from the database while rendering (they are in memory)' (docs/rules/storefront.md:69-71) and the read before the first request.
findings.done_when: The new unit test passes, and on production the calls of the ui_translations group-by statement in pg_stat_statements grow by fewer than 200 a day per running instance that serves no translated language (1,440 today).
findings.saving: Nine in ten of the per-minute queries for an instance that serves only hand-written languages: today about 3,570 a day falls to about 360. One query per cold start stays. No visible change.
findings.risk: Low. An instance that has served no translated language for a while learns of an edit within ten minutes instead of one; pages are cached for hours anyway, and reloadUi() refreshes the instance where the edit was made at once. If the chain's tick throws, the chain stops: catch inside the tick, as refresh() already does.
findings.notes: P3 because the cost is tiny; do it when ui-text.ts is opened for TX-3 or TX-12. The verified fix was to drop the timer and call ensureUi() from resolveShop(); I did not keep that, because ensureUi() reads Date.now(), which Next guards during prerender, and a page must not start or wait on a database read. The flag keeps the cost following use without either. DQ-12 and CA-12 propose a plainer form (ten minutes while the table has no language); this one also stays cheap once languages exist. SG-5 proposes splitting the reader (src/server/ui-load.ts) from the admin's tools so the start hook loads 208 modules instead of 856; these steps apply to whichever file holds the reader.

The ratchet for catalogues in client code reads only files that say 'use client' and import a catalogue directly (admin-catalogues.scan.test.ts:45-55), so it does not see templates-helpers.ts, store-features.ts or the lib modules that import a catalogue by value (68 outside the admin by my count). Nothing keeps the registry out of code outside the admin (TX-1). 14 catalogue files import code; notifications.en.ts bundled alone is 524 KB minified, of which 47 KB is its own text and 454 KB is zod (verified report). Nothing looks for keys no code names. The comment at ci.yml:35 names the catalogues as the reason for the 7 GB heap; measured alone they take about 125 MB.
findings.cost: No running cost of its own. It is how 3.6 MB of text reached 802 route entries and over half of two documents without a test going red.
findings.who_pays: Everyone who pays for TX-1, TX-2, TX-4, TX-5, TX-7 and TX-8 again later.
fix_steps: 1. Server reach: src/lib/admin-text-reach.scan.test.ts (TX-1 step 4): no value import of lib/admin-text outside the admin, and a ceiling on the catalogue files the proxy, /api/visit and the storefront layout reach, which only falls.
2. Visitor scripts: src/lib/storefront-bundle.scan.test.ts forbids lib/admin-messages (TX-8 step 3) and lib/known-cookies (TX-5 step 5).

3. Admin scripts: replace the matcher of admin-catalogues.scan.test.ts lines 45-55 with a walk that follows imports through modules without a directive (the walk of storefront-bundle.scan.test.ts; AC-11 writes it as src/components/admin/admin-bundle.scan.test.ts). Today's indirect import sites start as a list that may only shrink; lib/i18n and whole language modules join it after TX-7.

4. Catalogue files stay text: new src/lib/admin-messages/imports.scan.test.ts. A file of src/lib/admin-messages may import types, other catalogue files and a named list of plain label modules; today's value imports (36 in 14 files) are the starting list, which may only shrink, and zod is refused outright.

5. Dead keys: new src/lib/message-keys.scan.test.ts. It reads every leaf name of the storefront's English and the admin's English catalogues and every identifier in non-test files outside the catalogues, and fails for a key whose name appears nowhere. Tables read by a computed key or by matching English sentences are listed by their parent path (the problems tables of TX-10, option and state tables), not key by key; 192 key names sit in such tables today.
6. Documents: the document budget of TX-2 step 6 in e2e/signed-in/admin-scripts.spec.ts.
7. Correct the comment at .github/workflows/ci.yml:35: the whole program's type check needs the heap; the catalogues alone take about 125 MB.
8. One sentence each in CLAUDE.md (Conventions, beside the visitor's-scripts rule) and docs/performance.md: where the admin's words may be imported, and that a catalogue file imports no code.

src/lib/storefront-bundle.scan.test.ts: two more forbidden targets (step 2).

findings.title: English refusals are kept twice and matched back to their Norwegian by regular expression
findings.evidence: Server modules write refusals as English sentences; the catalogue repeats each as a template; words modules (known-words, marketing-words, discount-words, redirect-words and experiment-words among them) build one RegExp per entry and match the server's sentence to find the Norwegian. This is a written decision (D312 A6 and A8: the server answers in English because the AI manager and the tests read it). Ten tables hold 300 entries and 16.7 KB of English that also sits in code (verified report). For 19 entries no literal sentence is in the code, but at least 7 of those are built from parts and do match at run time (broadcasts.ts:40-45, settings.ts:70), so a text search cannot tell drift from design. One real gap, re-checked: the server says 'Use at most N videos.' and 'Use at most N 3D models.' (product-media.ts:60-61); no table carries those sentences, and the catalogue's product.media.tooManyVideos and tooManyModels ('A product has at most {n} videos.') are named by no code.
findings.cost: About 17 KB of English kept in two places with nothing checking that they still match. A refusal that stops matching reaches a Norwegian owner in English without any error. The run-time cost is negligible (about 300 regular expressions built once per instance).
findings.who_pays: An owner who reads an untranslated refusal; whoever edits a sentence in one place only.
fix_steps: 1. A guard that tests real refusals, not text: one test per words module (beside it, for example src/lib/marketing-words.coverage.test.ts) calls the module's validators with input that fails each rule and asserts every refusal returned is matched by an entry (knownText(refusal, english, nb) differs from the refusal). Start with broadcasts (src/lib/broadcasts.ts), discounts, redirects, experiments and the tax and payments settings.

2. The product media pair: either add the two sentences of product-media.ts:60-61 to the table the product editor matches and delete product.media.tooManyVideos and tooManyModels, or make mediaProblems() say the catalogue's sentences. Decide with TX-11, which lists the two keys as unread.

3. Only if step 1 keeps turning up drift: the server answers with a code and values, and both the English for the AI manager and the Norwegian come from the catalogue entry. That changes tool answers, so the AI eval recording must be made again.
tests_and_rules: src/lib/product-media.test.ts:19-20 asserts the two English sentences.
src/lib/admin-messages/tax-payments.test.ts and tax-reports.test.ts hold parts of the tax tables.
Rule kept: D312 A6 and A8 (the server answers in English; screens say it from the catalogue's problems by matching). Step 3 would change A8 and needs the decision recorded in docs/decisions.md.
src/data/agent-eval-recording.json: only step 3 would require a new recording.
depends_on: TX-11 for the two product.media keys
findings.done_when: The coverage tests of step 1 pass for the five validators named, and product.media has no entry that no code reads (rg tooManyVideos outside the catalogues finds a reader, or the keys are gone).
findings.saving: No measurable bytes or time. The gain is no silent English for a Norwegian owner. The full change (step 3) would remove about 17 KB of duplicated source.
findings.risk: A guard based on text search would raise false alarms on sentences built from parts; the guard here calls the validators instead. Step 3 must keep the English the AI manager reads word for word, or the eval recording changes.
findings.notes: P3: a true duplicate, but a deliberate one with no running cost. Worth step 1 when one of these validators is next changed. DD-7 (unused-code) describes the neighbouring case of English constants kept beside the catalogues and held equal by tests.

findings.title: 34 texts that no code reads

Admin: domains.checkout.priceChanged, platformTools.aiActions.noTemplate, analytics.settings.targets.startCustom, inventory.documents.linesCol, inventory.suppliers.sentWithin, reviews.import.submitCheck, order.messages.refundReason and cancelReason, blog.editor.blogHeading, oauth.store.cutDone, customers.saved.schema.wholePercent and oneAccount, marketing.segments.firstBy, assistant.autopilot.plans.pausedNow, content.entry.publishFirstSave, product.media.tooManyVideos and tooManyModels. Storefront: returns.chooseLines, returns.returnRequest.pickLines, workInvoice.creditPageTitle, deliveryChoice.deliveryLine, affiliate.cartApplied, affiliate.signInToRefer, creator.ordersLabel, companyAccount.decidedAlready, tracking.followAt, nothingHere, allArticles, subscriptionOrders, account.resetFor, account.passwordShort, stay.tooSoon, stay.tooFar, giftCardLine.notDiscounted. I searched the 32 names other than the product.media pair in src, e2e, scripts and wordpress-plugin: none has a reader; affiliate.cartApplied is named by one test (affiliate-text.test.ts:27). The 8 entries of marketing.problems and payments.problems on the first list are live and are not on this one.

findings.who_pays: Whoever writes and translates the catalogues; the AI translation of each new language; a few bytes in every function.

High for the 8 matching-table entries if someone deletes them from the older list: nothing would fail, the refusal would just read English.

findings.title: Every instance start reads every AI-translated language whole, one after another, and builds it before the first request
findings.evidence: refresh() loops over the languages in the table and awaits loadLanguage() for each in turn (ui-text.ts:63-70). loadLanguage() reads every key of the language, interface and email (line 48), and at once builds two full message objects with overlayMessages() and a third copy for the browser (lines 52-53). startUi() awaits all of it (line 108) and Next holds requests until register() returns. So with L translated languages every new instance runs L + 1 statements one after another and builds L languages, whatever it will serve: a health check, a cron run, a store that sells only in Norwegian. Measured with the real overlayMessages() on a stand-in language of English length: 1,863 rows (1,673 interface, 190 email), 134,820 bytes as JSON; 13 ms for the first language and 5.6 ms on average; 443 KB of heap kept per language, of which the rows alone are 229 KB. The languages are the platform's (commerce.platform_languages), not a store's, so L is the number of languages anyone has had translated.
findings.cost: Nothing today: no language is translated before opening. Per translated language afterwards, at every cold start of every instance: one more round trip to the database before the first request (its time was not measured), about 135 KB of rows, 6 to 13 ms of CPU and 0.44 MB of heap. With 20 languages (the EU's other official languages) that is 21 statements in a row, about 2.7 MB of rows, 0.1 to 0.26 s of CPU and about 9 MB of heap per cold start (estimate: the one-language measurement times 20). The cost follows the platform's number of languages, not what the instance serves.
findings.who_pays: The server at every cold start; a shopper whose request starts an instance; the database.
fix_steps: 1. One statement for the languages that changed. In refresh() (ui-text.ts:57-72) collect the languages whose version differs, then read them together: select lang, key, text from commerce.ui_translations where lang = any(...) (textList() from src/server/sql-arrays.ts), and group the rows by language in code. Two statements at start instead of L + 1.

2. Build a language when it is first read. src/lib/ui-registry.ts: an entry may hold makers beside values (makeUi and makeEmail, each a function); registeredUi(lang) and registeredEmail(lang) call the maker on first read, keep the result and drop the maker. loadLanguage() registers makers that close over the two maps and call overlayMessages("ui", t("en"), ui, lang) and overlayMessages("email", emailText("en"), email, lang). t() stays synchronous and never waits on the database: the rows are already in memory. The browser's UiTexts keeps registering values as today.
3. Keep for the browser only what TX-3 hands (the 114 browser keys and the withdrawal page's 144), not a third copy of every text (line 53).
4. forgetMessages() and reloadUi() work as before: a reload registers fresh makers. Update the module comment (ui-text.ts:19-27).

5. Not now, and only if cold starts show it once there are many languages: load a language's rows on first need instead of at start, awaited where a store is read (getStore() in src/server/stores.ts:199 already notes per-store facts on each call) and before emails (ensureUi()). 124 files call t() with a language taken from data, so one missed path would show English and a cached page could keep it; that risk is why this step waits.
tests_and_rules: New unit test of the loader with a counting stub for readDb() and a spy on overlayMessages(): with three translated languages, the start issues 2 statements and builds nothing; t("de") then builds one language once; a second t("de") builds nothing.
src/server/languages.int.test.ts (lines 123-131, 176) and src/server/ui-nightly.int.test.ts read translated text back through t() and uiTextsFor(): they must stay green unchanged.
src/lib/ui-catalog.test.ts: overlayMessages() itself does not change.
Rules kept: 'never read the texts from the database while rendering (they are in memory)' (docs/rules/storefront.md:69-71) and the read before the first request (src/instrumentation.ts:1-5).
depends_on: TX-3 (same lines of loadLanguage(); do them together)
findings.done_when: The new unit test passes: with three translated languages startUi() issues 2 statements (4 as written today) and overlayMessages() is not called until t() is first read for a language.
findings.saving: Per translated language that an instance does not serve: one round trip fewer before the first request, about 4 to 11 ms of CPU and about 0.2 MB of heap (measured here: 5.6 to 13 ms and 443 KB today against 1.5 ms and 229 KB when only the rows are kept). At 20 languages: 19 round trips, roughly 0.1 to 0.2 s and 4 MB per cold start (estimate by multiplication). Nothing today.
findings.risk: Low. The first page in a language pays its 6 to 13 ms of building once per instance, during the render, as pure CPU. A maker that throws would throw inside t(): build inside try and fall back to English, as a failed read does today. The grouped read returns all changed languages in one answer (about 135 KB each); at start that is every language, which is the same data as today in one statement.
findings.notes: Added by the planner's completeness pass. It is not an argument about the feature and does not rest on the empty table: it is what every instance will pay per language once stores use it, and before opening is the cheapest time to change it because no language exists yet. SG-5 (server graph) covers the other half of the same start hook: it loads 856 modules to do this read; split the reader from the admin's tools there and apply these steps to the reader. DQ-12 covers the every-minute poll (TX-6 here).
